comment: Golden vectors for the recursively closed runtime configuration surface. The schema travels with the cases as machine-readable data: a 493-line contract every implementer hand-transcribes is one they will transcribe differently. A conforming validator consumes 'nodes' and must accept every case in 'cases' and refuse every case in 'reject_cases' with the declared reason at the declared path.
closure_rule: Every object node admits exactly its declared keys, at every depth. An undeclared key is unknown_key. A map node is open in its keys and closed in the shape of every value. A delegated node is closed against the named external schema, never open.

cases.name: complete_valid_document
cases.note: Every node exercised at least once, so the schema is shown to be satisfiable rather than merely restrictive.

reject_cases.name: unknown_key_at_the_root
reject_cases.note: The shallowest case. A v1 runtime would accept and ignore this.

reject_cases.name: unknown_key_inside_gateway_auth
reject_cases.note: Two levels down. This is the case that separates a recursive schema from one that closes only its top level.

reject_cases.name: unknown_key_four_levels_down
reject_cases.note: actions.sms.incoming_webhook.signature is the deepest object in the surface. A schema that closes three levels and stops is closed nowhere that matters, because this is where an authentication setting would be quietly weakened.

reject_cases.name: relocated_rated_capacity_amps
reject_cases.note: Not a typo and not an unrecognised setting: a real field that now belongs to the commissioning authority. Reporting it as unknown would have an operator delete it rather than move it.

reject_cases.name: unknown_key_inside_a_declared_map_value
reject_cases.note: A declared map is open in its keys and closed in the shape of every value. Operators name commands; they do not extend what a command is.

reject_cases.name: delegated_config_key_the_manifest_does_not_declare
reject_cases.note: Delegation closes rather than opens. A skill's config surface is bounded by its own manifest, so this is refused against that schema and not waved through as somebody else's problem.

reject_cases.name: wrong_type_for_a_declared_scalar
reject_cases.note: A declared key carrying the wrong type is not an unknown key, and saying so points at the value rather than the name.

reject_cases.name: boolean_where_an_integer_is_declared
reject_cases.note: JSON separates booleans from numbers and some languages do not; in Python True is an instance of int, so a naive check accepts this.

reject_cases.name: out_of_range_exclusive_minimum
reject_cases.note: retry_interval_minutes must be greater than zero, not merely non-negative.

reject_cases.name: value_outside_a_closed_vocabulary
reject_cases.note: An enum is a closed vocabulary like any other node.

reject_cases.name: required_key_absent
reject_cases.note: device.id is what a runtime is. Its absence is a different failure from a wrong value.

reject_cases.name: required_calibration_key_absent
reject_cases.note: Calibration values have no defaults on purpose: a guessed one produces a plausible number rather than a measurement.

reject_cases.name: pattern_violation
reject_cases.note: An env var name that is not one would fail at lookup instead of at load.
